phase: W2a PR 1a: the film, the lift for point contacts on the plane and the tube, the roughness cutoff, the coupling report; gates 1-4 and 7-12
labels: predictions by W2a's builder from F0's hand-over spike (plans' C3: the lift form within about 7 % to s/R 0.3, 15 to 19 % at 0.45 to 0.6), the first step's probe (run 42794134037: the coarse MRS's error at the hand-over gap by blob, the film's increment semidefinite in 2,000 draws, float32 within 5e-4 of the increment's scale) and one smoke run through the node (below, seen before)

operating_point.platform: CPU: CI's default lane, and GitHub runners (4 vCPU) for the probes
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: a sphere of radius a = 1 mm, water (1 mPa s), a plane wall z = 0 (and a straight tube of radius 2 mm for the tube arms); the drag's spacing s/a 0.15, 0.2 and 0.3, blob 0.05 (the lubricated default) unless stated; h_m = 0.75 s; roughness 1 nm on both surfaces for the oracle gates (cutoff 1.4 nm, far below every gap judged), the default 1 um for gate 12
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: gate 4: poses drawn at physical scales (gap 1e-3 to 1 radius, any orientation), 200 draws a body kind; controls' rates on Actions with .github/probe/detection_rate.py

gate_1_sphere_plane_exact.claim: the lubricated drag's 6 x 6 for a sphere above a plane lies within the stated line of the exact resistance at every gap judged
gate_1_sphere_plane_exact.kind: bounds (against exact answers: Brenner's series on the normal, the method of fundamental solutions on the rest)
gate_1_sphere_plane_exact.case: tests/oracles/test_lubrication.py::test_gate1_*, the drag node's own step at each gap

prediction.unit: relative error of each diagonal entry; couplings on sqrt(R_ii R_jj)
prediction.basis: measured-before (the hand-over spike: within about 7 % to s/R 0.3) and the smoke run's normal entry
prediction.why: the error is the coarse MRS's at h_m (3.5-4.2 % at blob 0.05) plus the film's form error at h_m / R (about 3 % at 0.1 R, 8 % at 0.2 R on the sphere): s/a 0.15 and 0.2 put h_m at 0.11 and 0.15 radii

gate_1_sphere_plane_exact.lines: s/a 0.15 and 0.2: 7 % per entry at every gap; s/a 0.3 (h_m 0.225 R, past WINDOW, handover_window raised): 12 %
gate_1_sphere_plane_exact.metric: per-entry relative error (the normal against Brenner at every gap, the shear entries against the MFS at h/a >= 0.06 where it resolves to 2e-4)

control.plant: (a) the lift omitted (lubrication=False, the coarse MRS alone); (b) the film's increment x1.1 (the dev2 plan's 'every log coefficient x1.1')
control.expected_rate: (a) 1/1 at every gap below h_m (the coarse MRS alone 22 to 147 % off or indefinite there); (b) caught at the gaps where 10 % of the increment exceeds the line less the measured error: predicted h/a <= 0.02 on the normal, not at 0.05 on the rotation (S4's caveat), the range stated per entry
control.resolution: the MFS's 2e-4; the gate is silent on (b) above the gaps where it does not catch it

gate_1_sphere_plane_exact.cannot_discriminate_if: a hard max in place of the smooth lift: equally accurate away from h_m; gate 8 carries it

gate_2_coupling.claim: a sphere spun on a flat wall in still fluid translates at the exact rate per rotation at every gap down to the cutoff (the hydrodynamic half of the rolling arm's stage 1)
gate_2_coupling.case: U / (a Omega) = -(R_FU^-1 R_FOmega) from the node's 6 x 6, against the MFS's at h/a >= 0.06

prediction.unit: relative error of the translation per rotation
prediction.basis: guess from gate 1's line: the coupling's error over the tangential's
prediction.why: the ratio of two entries each within gate 1's line

control.plant: the film's coupling block added twice (the double count M4's lesson names)
control.expected_rate: N/N at gaps where the film's coupling exceeds 10 % of the total's (predicted h/a <= 0.1)

gate_3_form_oracles.claim: the film's form: the normal entry's local exponent in the gap is -1 for a sphere and -3/2 for a line contact; the h -> 0 limit of the sphere's normal R_zz h / (6 pi mu a^2) is 1
gate_3_form_oracles.kind: estimates (form oracles: O3's exponent, limit and windowed exponent)
gate_3_form_oracles.case: the node's normal entry at gaps 1e-3 to 1e-2 a (roughness 1 nm), and the film alone on a line contact (k2 = 0)

prediction.basis: derived (Reynolds on the paraboloid) and measured-before (the spike's 0.02 % on the normal, 0.2-0.5 % on the line contact)
prediction.why: the increment carries the leading singular term exactly; the coarse MRS's share is O(1)

control.plant: (a) a sphere law on a line contact (k2 = k1); (b) the radius off by two (curvatures halved)
control.expected_rate: (a) N/N by the exponent; (b) N/N by the limit (reads near 4); the windowed exponent's dev1-blend control is not run here: the blend is the surrogate's, not this rung's

gate_4_definiteness.claim: the lift form is positive definite wherever the coarse MRS at the opened geometry is
gate_4_definiteness.case: a sphere and an ellipsoid above a plane and in a tube, poses drawn (gap 1e-3 to 1 a, any orientation), the node's least scaled eigenvalue

prediction.basis: measured-before (0 of 19,407 in the hand-over spike; the increment 0 of 2,000 in the first step)

control.plant: the increment's normal entry negated (an indefinite increment)
control.expected_rate: N/N: the node replaces the resistance by NaN and the run stops (drag.mrs-indefinite)

gate_7_x2_control.claim: the register's M4 control: the lubrication term scaled x2 moves the body's speed by the amount the 6 x 6 predicts
gate_7_x2_control.kind: equality (a linear algebra identity through the node, to rounding)
gate_7_x2_control.case: a sphere settling towards the plane under a constant force: the speed with the increment x2 against (R_MRS(opened) + 2 dTF)^-1 F from the node's own reported film_increment and resistance

control.expected_rate: N/N: the speed then misses the x2 prediction by the term's share

gate_8_gradients.claim: forward and reverse derivatives agree with central differences across h = h_m and across the roughness cutoff, through the plane's offset, the tube's radius and the body's position, and through a run_scan of several steps

control.plant: (a) a stop_gradient on the opening's dependence on the gap; (b) a hard max in place of the smooth lift
control.expected_rate: (a) N/N at gaps below h_m; (b) the derivative jumps at h_m: N/N on a sweep through it

gate_9_practical_differentiability.claim: the two-builds check is quiet on the lubricated step: no build-time number is baked into its program (the search's numbers and the hand-over spacing are leaves)

control.plant: the hand-over gap made a constant of the program

gate_10_bits_dtypes.claim: every released program (drag 0.3.0, 0.4.0, and 0.5.0's surrogate) is bit for bit in both dtypes; the lubricated 6 x 6 in float32 lies within 1e-3 of float64's on its diagonal scale

prediction.unit: float32 against float64, on the diagonal scale
prediction.basis: measured-before (the film's increment 5e-4 worst; the coarse MRS 5e-6)

bits.cases: released programs through .github/probe/bit_compare.py, base 1ea44ea against the head, one CPU

gate_11_never_silent.claim: a film solve that is not finite or whose residual exceeds FILM_RESIDUAL_ULPS ulps is flagged (film_unsolved) on every step of every run, forward and in a gradient's forward pass

control.plant: the film's elimination scaled by 1.01 (a wrong solve, residual about 1e-2)
control.expected_rate: N/N runs, every step flagged; 0/N with nothing planted

gate_12_cutoff_exposure.claim: roughness_cutoff (the public reader standing for W2b's traction law) returns the cutoff the film uses; moving a surface's roughness moves the film's normal force below the cutoff by the predicted ratio; the film is continuous in value and slope through the cutoff
gate_12_cutoff_exposure.kind: equality (the reader), estimates (the ratio), equality to resolution (continuity)

prediction.unit: relative miss of the predicted ratio (the film's leading 1/h at the floored gap)

control.plant: the floor's gap taken from the body's roughness alone
control.expected_rate: N/N: the reader's value then differs from the film's

costs.prediction: a lubricated step near the wall costs two film solves more than the coarse MRS's (about 5-6 ms each on a runner at 65 nodes) plus the contact's search; beyond h_m plus its width it costs only the search
costs.measured_at: the first-step probe's film-grid arm; the gate size is measured by node_measure.py through the node
